scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "1000000000: un miliardo;", "1000000000000: un bilione;": Italian counts in the long scale.; Treccani, "bilione": "corrispondente a un milione di milioni, cioè a mille miliardi".

group_mark.source: CLDR 48 it number symbols (ICU 78 formats 1234567.5 as "1.234.567,5"): the dot groups digits.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR 48 it number symbols (ICU 78 formats 1234567.5 as "1.234.567,5"): the comma marks the decimals.

space_groups.source: CLDR 48 it number symbols group digits with a dot, so a space separates two numbers.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: "milioni di persone" names no number; "due milioni" does.

scale_noun_agrees.source: A scale noun agrees in number with its count. Treccani, "Numerali": "di milione, miliardo, bilione, ecc., che hanno un regolare plurale e che, per indicare una quantità determinata, devono essere necessariamente preceduti da un altro cardinale"; "(5) in Asia vivono quasi quattro miliardi di persone".

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it %spellout-numbering: "20: vent>%%msco-with-i>;": the unit follows the ten in one word, with no joiner.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "100: cent>%%msc-with-o>;": the rest follows "cento" in one word, with no joiner.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "1000001: un milione >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;"; speech also joins groups with "e" ("un milione e duecentomila"); reading accepts both.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: Treccani, "mille": "milleuno, milledue... millecento (o mille e uno, mille e due, mille e cento)": after "mille e" a well-formed last group is below a hundred or a round hundred.

small_multiplier_starts_group.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF it data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 1100 and 2100: "millecento", "duemilacento": the hundred after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred multiplier counts no group of thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: The CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it rules quoted for joiner_between_groups write no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: Treccani, "mille": "milleuno, milledue... millecento (o mille e uno, mille e due, mille e cento)": the last group follows "mille" with or without "e".

ordinal_style.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it %spellout-ordinal-masculine: "200: <%spellout-cardinal-masculine<­cent>%%ordinal-esimo-with-o>;": only the end of an ordinal is ordinal.

compound_words.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) it %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "2001: <%%msc-no-final<­mila­>%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;": the words of a number below a million are one word ("duemilacinquecento"), so a word splits into number words.; Treccani, "mille": "milleuno, milledue... millecento [...] millecentouno, millecentocinquanta".

clock_before.source: it.wikipedia "Sistema orario a 24 ore": "quello corrispondente alle 23:59". An hour and minutes written with a point next to "alle" are a time of day, not a decimal.

joiner.source: "e" joins a half ("due e mezzo", "un milione e mezzo") and, in speech, the groups ("un milione e duecentomila").

minus_idioms.source: Treccani, "quanto" 3 c (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/issue-fixes/163/sources/treccani-quanto.txt): "q. meno (anche, non com., in una parola: quantomeno), al minimo, almeno". "più o meno due" is "about two", not -2: in these idioms "meno" is an adverb.

percent_phrase.source: Treccani, "cento" 3: "espressioni come il tre per cento, il cinquanta per cento, ecc. (scritto 3%, 50%, ecc.) indicano frazioni il cui denominatore è 100, cioè valori percentuali". So "cento" after "per" names the percent sign, not the number 100.

article_one.source: "un", "uno" and "una" are also the indefinite article; alone before a noun they are a weak number.

of.source: "un milione di persone": "di" after a scale noun; a plural collective after it multiplies the count. en.wiktionary (Italian) "del": "contraction of di + il"; "dello": "di lo"; "della": "di la"; "dei": "di i"; "degli": "di gli"; "delle": "di le"; "dell'" before a vowel.

fraction_of.source: "un terzo di dozzina": a fraction of a collective noun multiplies it.

denominator_particle.source: Italian has no particle like pt "avos".

class_noun.source: No Italian class noun is read.

half_unit.source: "e mezzo" follows the noun in Italian ("un chilo e mezzo").

lone_decimal_mark.source: Structural, no external source: a group mark stands only between digits, so a point right before the first digit marks decimals, as in pt-PT: ".5" is 0.5. CLDR 48 it number symbols: decimal ",", so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Treccani, "tra": "ci incontreremo tra le sei e le otto, o nell’intervallo tra il primo e il secondo atto".

roman_title.source: A regnal title before a name makes the Roman numeral after the name a regnal number (Wikipedia, "Regnal number": "Regnal numbers are ordinal numbers—often written as Roman numerals—used to distinguish among persons with the same regnal name who held the same office, notably kings, queens regnant, popes"). Each title, from en.wiktionary.org: Italian "papa": "pope"; Italian "re": "king (male monarch)"; Italian "regina": "queen (monarch)"; Italian "imperatore": "emperor"; Italian "imperatrice": "empress".

roman_word.source: A Roman numeral that is also a word or a common abbreviation reads only after a strong cue ("Play CD" holds no 400). Each word, from en.wiktionary.org unless another dictionary is named: Translingual "XL": "(chiefly clothing) extra large (the manufactured size)"; Translingual "mm": "(metrology) Symbol for millimetre (millimeter), an SI unit of length equal to 10−3 metres (meters)."; Translingual "cm": "(metrology) Symbol for centimeter (centimetre), an SI unit of length equal to 10−2 meters (metres)."; Translingual "ml": "(metrology) Symbol for millilitre, an SI unit of fluid measure equal to 10−3 litres."; Italian "di": "used to indicate possession, after the thing owned and before the owner; of; ’s"; Italian "ci": "us"; Italian "li": "(accusative) them (masculine)"; Italian "mi": "clitic accusative of io. me".

roman_lower_word.source: A Roman numeral that is also a word in lower case only: the lower-case word reads only after a strong cue, and the upper-case numeral reads like any other ("Felipe VI"). Each word, from en.wiktionary.org: Italian "vi": "second-person personal plural object pronoun: you, to you".
